title: Idempotency, retries and deliberately testing the error path

videos.script: Somebody presses Buy on a slow connection. Nothing happens, so they press it again. {{double-tap}} Did they buy one ticket or two? That question is this lesson. boxoffice answers it with an idempotency key. Send the same key twice, and the second answer is a copy of the first. {{key}} Then retries. Some failures are worth trying again, and some never are. A 422 will fail the same way forever. A 503 might work in a second. {{retry}} You will write a small retry helper, and test it without any server at all. {{helper}} Then the error path, on purpose. The payment is declined, the provider is down, the provider is too slow. {{errors}} After each one, you check what boxoffice left behind. {{seats}} Then a defect. Two requests with the same key, at the same moment, buy twice. You will catch it with a test and write it up. {{race}} Last, timeouts. A timeout does not say the payment failed. It says nobody knows. {{timeout}} By the end you test the paths where things go wrong, and that is where most of the money is lost.
